summary: The single Hebrew occurrence describes foreigners leaving their strongholds after hearing of the king. In the parallel song a differently ordered verb describes their emergence.

senses.definition: The foreigners lose heart and emerge from their fortified places. The surrounding clauses describe their fear and submission to the victorious king.

note: Arabic ḫaraja supports the possibility of outward movement; fear comes from the Hebrew context. With only one biblical use, the relative force of movement and trembling remains uncertain (compare 2Sa.22.46).
